TERMS OF USE: https://future.lxcat.net/scat-cs/inspect?ids=2079492,2079574,2079616,2079700,2079745,2079790,2079835,2079880,2079925,2079970,2080015,2080060,2080150,2080216,2080261,2080306,2394132,2932623,2933135,4141307,4195629&termsOfUse=true

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
DATABASE:         IST-Lisbon
DESCRIPTION:      S Baghel, L Marques and L L Alves, ''Cross-sections for H2 and NH3 relevant to N2-H2 plasma modelling” 2026 Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. (submitted). The complete cross sections set was compiled mostly from Hayashi personal communication to the JILA Atomic Collisions Data Center, 1987, for momentum-transfer and vibrational excitation; R. Snoeckx et al 2023 Plasma Sources Science and Technology 32 115020, for electronic excitation; P. Rawat et al 2008 International Journal of Mass Spectrometry, 277 96, for attachment; and R. Rejoub 2001 The Journal of Chemical Physics, 115 5053, for ionization. All cross sections are defined up to at least 1 keV, with some extended up to 3 keV. When this complete set is used in a two-term Boltzmann solver (choosing a linear interpolation scheme), it yields calculated swarm parameters in good agreement with measurements for E/N values between 1 and 400 Td. For E/N < 1 Td, the set must be further completed to include rotational excitation mechanisms (see below), in order to reproduce measured swarm data.
IMPORTANT NOTICE ABOUT ROTATIONAL TRANSITIONS
This set is to be completed with the rotational cross sections for transitions NH3(X,v=0,J=0) <--> NH3(X,v=0,J’) (J’=1-5), available in this database under group NH2-rot (see NH3-rot description for more details). When the full cross section set for NH3 (containing momentum-transfer, vibrational excitation, and electronic excitation and ionization from ground-state) and NH3-rot (including the rotational excitation/deexcitation between NH3(J=0) and NH3(J=1-5) states) are used in a two-term Boltzmann solver, one obtains calculated swarm parameters in good agreement with measurements over a large range of E/N values (1e-4 to 400 Td).
